note: Published statements used in check 2, quoted as fetched on 2026-11-14. 'derived' is this fixture's reading of the quote in UTC, with the precision the wording supports.

sources.what: Blue Ghost Mission 1: end of daylight on 16 March 2025
quotes: completing more than 14 days of surface operations (346 hours of daylight), and operating just over 5 hours into the lunar night with the final data received around 6:15 pm CDT on March 16
Firefly also captured imagery of the lunar sunset on March 16
Following the sunset, Blue Ghost operated for 5 hours into the lunar night
sources.derived: Final data about 23:15 UTC (6:15 pm CDT = UTC-5). 'Just over 5 hours' of night before that puts the start of night at about 18:15 UTC or a little earlier. Independently, 346 h after the 08:34 UTC touchdown is 18:34 UTC. So: night began around 18:15-18:35 UTC on 16 March, to within a few tens of minutes ('around', 'just over', whole hours). The release does not say what 'sunset' means (first contact, last limb, or loss of power).

sources.what: Blue Ghost Mission 1: the 14 March 2025 eclipse as seen from the landing site
sources.publisher: KUT Radio (Austin NPR station), report by Kailey Hunt, published 2025-03-14 4:00 PM CDT, citing Firefly
quotes: The solar eclipse lasted nearly five hours, starting at 12 a.m. CST and ending around 4:52 a.m. at the Blue Ghost's landing site in the Mare Crisium
Totality lasted just over 2 hours, beginning at 1:18 a.m.
Another image, taken around 3:30 a.m., shows the lunar lander capturing a "diamond ring effect," as the sun prepared to emerge from totality behind Earth.
sources.derived: Read as US Central Daylight Time (UTC-5), which was in force in Texas on that date and is the zone of the article's own time stamp and of Firefly's caption: eclipse 05:00 to about 09:52 UTC, totality from 06:18 UTC for 'just over 2 hours', Sun about to re-emerge around 08:30 UTC. The article writes 'CST' once; taken literally (UTC-6) every time would be one hour later. Precision: one minute for 1:18 and 4:52, 'around' for the rest.

sources.what: Firefly's caption for the diamond-ring image
quotes: Captured at our landing site in the Moon's Mare Crisium around 3:30 am CDT, the photo shows the sun about to emerge from totality behind Earth.
sources.derived: About 08:30 UTC, just before the end of totality.

sources.what: Chandrayaan-3: next sunrise at the landing site
sources.publisher: ISRO post of 2023-09-02, as reproduced by The News Minute
quotes: The solar panel is oriented to receive the light at the next sunrise expected on September 22, 2023.

sources.what: Chandrayaan-3: status after the lunar day
quotes: September 04, 2023 The lander and rover are in sleep mode. Awaiting their awakening around September 22, 2023.
Knowing that the Sun would set at Shivshakti point on September 4, the scientists began a phased shutdown of the two devices on September 2.

sources.what: Apollo 11-17: altitude and azimuth of the Sun and Earth at landing, at the start and end of each EVA and at lift-off (37 instants)
sources.publisher: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (NASA), table by Jim Scotti; copy in events/alsj_scotti_altaz.txt
quotes: e-lon and e-lat are the sub-Earth longitude and latitudes derived from interpolating the Nautical Almanac lunar ephemeris data. e-Alt and e-Az are the Altitude and Azimuth of the Earth at that time.
sources.derived: Values to 0.01 deg, computed from sub-Earth and sub-solar points, i.e. directions from the Moon's centre: Earth's altitude therefore lacks the site parallax (up to 0.26 deg).
